subject: Re: POC trial plan and deployment mode \u0014 Acme Corp
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC recap + next steps  deployment mode decision

Hi John / Samantha 

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the PoC aligned with Acme's deployment constraints and success criteria.

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary objective: validate model throughput and latency for your document-understanding workflow (legal docs ingestion, Q&A).
- Data sensitivity: some PII in sample dataset  you flagged needing either Dedicated capacity with VPC peering or Private (VPC/on-prem) for the production rollout.
- Stakeholders: Samantha (Platform), Raj Patel (Security  not on call), Legal to review DPIA.

Options we discussed:
1) Hosted API (fastest turn-up)  minimal onboarding, not suitable if you need customer-managed keys or strict network isolation.
2) Dedicated capacity  reserved GPU pool with customer tenancy; supports VPC peering and KMS integration; good middle ground for performance + isolation.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem)  full control, longer lead time, suitable for regulated data.

Proposed PoC/trial plan (high level):
- Scope: run 1-week performance run using a representative 10k-document sample and your canonical prompts.
- Success criteria (examples): p95 latency < 200ms for short queries, end-to-end throughput >= X docs/min, output quality within your baseline evals, and no PII exfiltration in logs.
- Timeline: kickoff within 1-2 weeks, short 4-week PoC (config + run + review) unless you need Private deployment which can add 3-6 weeks for network/KMS setup.
- Who we need from your side: platform lead (Samantha), security reviewer (Raj), and one ML/engineering contact for dataset access.

I've attached a draft Mutual Action Plan and your security questionnaire backfilled with our placeholder answers. Can you confirm which deployment mode you'd like to prioritize for the PoC (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC) and any changes to the success criteria or timeline?

If Dedicated is the preference, Ben (cc'd) will suggest a concrete PoC runbook and a proposed kickoff slot next week.

Thanks  happy to jump on a 20-30 minute follow-up if that helps.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Acme_PoC_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx; security-questionnaire.pdf

Hi Lauren 

Thanks for the clear recap. After chatting with Samantha, Acme's preference for the PoC is to prioritize Dedicated capacity with VPC peering. Main reasons: predictable performance for our latency-sensitive APIs, and the ability to enforce KMS for keys during the trial.

A few questions / constraints from our side:
- Commitment: what is the minimum duration and estimated cost for a Dedicated PoC?
- Timeline: we'd like to get a technical kickoff within the next two weeks and run the PoC over ~4 weeks, with a view to production in Q4 if results look good.
- Security: Raj will need SOC2 evidence and our security questionnaire answered (we got the stub you attached  will confirm changes).

Stakeholders to include: Samantha Lee (Platform), Raj Patel (Security)  I'll introduce Raj once we confirm scope. Also cc'ing Ben if he wants to propose the runbook.

Can you confirm proposed kickoff slots next Tue/Wed?

Cheers,

Subject: Re: POC recap + next steps  Dedicated PoC runbook (draft)

Hi John 

Thanks  glad to hear Dedicated with VPC peering is the preferred path. Quick technical plan below; happy to walk through on a kickoff call.

Proposed Dedicated PoC runbook (draft):
1) Prep (Week 0)
   - Confirm dataset access and PII-scope (S3/share access).
   - Exchange network details for VPC peering and KMS key ARN (we support AWS KMS/HSM).
   - Access list and IAM roles for Redwood service accounts.
2) Deploy (Week 1)
   - Provision Dedicated GPU pool (reserved for your org) and configure VPC peering.
   - Deploy the chosen model variant with quantization profile we discussed.
3) Run (Week 2)
   - Ingest representative 10k-doc sample, run evaluation harness (latency, throughput, quality).
   - Enable KV/prefix caching to simulate steady-state.
4) Review (Week 3)
   - Joint review of metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, qualitative evals on a holdout set.
   - Action items for production rollout (KMS rotation, retention policy, routing).

Success criteria (to be finalized with you):
- p95 inference latency < 200ms for short requests (<= 128 tokens)
- Throughput consistent with baseline: at least 300 concurrent requests at target latency
- Model output quality: F1/accuracy vs your labeled eval within 5% of baseline
- No logs contain raw PII (we'll show how we strip/route logs)
- Cost target: (we'll propose a target number once we confirm model/config)

Estimated PoC duration: 4 weeks from kickoff assuming Dedicated provisioning. If you opt for Private VPC/on-prem, add 3-6 weeks for network approvals and access provisioning.

Proposed kickoff slots (PST): Tue 2026-07-21 10:00-10:30, Tue 2026-07-21 15:00-15:30, Wed 2026-07-22 11:00-11:30. Please confirm what works.

I've attached a short PoC_runbook.md and will update it after your feedback.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
